CAD, Postprocessing, Decision Support, Dose and Contrast Management, and Modality Structured Reports

Unit 1: Imaging Informatics Foundations. Lesson 7 of 65 in CIIP Academy.

The breast imaging group wants computer-aided detection results to appear next to the mammogram. Other groups ask for 3D reformats, dose tracking, and a clinical decision support prompt at order entry. Each is an add-on system, and each is only as good as how its output travels.

How the add-ons connect

Add-on                      Input                 Output travels as
CAD (breast, lung, prostate) images from PACS     DICOM SR or secondary capture
Postprocessing server       image series          new series, key images
Decision support            order or protocol     alert in EMR or RIS
Dose management             dose SR from modality dose registry record
Contrast management         injector data         record in the study or EMR
Ultrasound and DXA reports  modality structured   values flow into the report
                            reports
Artificial intelligence     images from PACS      result object, worklist flag

Computer-aided detection and postprocessing

CAD marks areas for the radiologist to consider; it is a second look, not a diagnosis. Its marks come back as a structured report or a secondary capture image. Postprocessing software and servers build multiplanar and 3D views from the stored slices and save the results as new series.

Decision support

Decision support works at order entry (is the exam appropriate?), at protocoling, and during interpretation (a case comparison with similar studies).

Dose and contrast

A dose structured report from the modality feeds a dose registry so exams can be compared with reference levels. Contrast dose data should land in the record too.

Artificial intelligence

At recognition level: an AI tool is another consumer of images and producer of results, so it needs a route in, a route out, and a place in the worklist.

Exam tip: ask where the output goes. A result with no storage object and no worklist flag will never be seen by the reader.
Remember
CAD, postprocessing, decision support, dose and contrast tracking, and AI tools are add-on systems whose value depends on how their results are stored and surfaced in the reading workflow.
Deeper explanation

CAD, Postprocessing, Decision Support, Dose and Contrast Management, and Modality Structured Reports, explained slowly

Following the output of an add-on

Every add-on starts well and fails in the same place: the result has nowhere to go. Trace output for each tool you deploy.

Tool                 Result object            Stored where            Shown to the reader by
CAD for mammography  structured report        PACS, with the study    overlay marks on the image
Lung nodule CAD      secondary capture        PACS                    extra series in the study
3D server            new series               PACS                    hanging protocol rule
Dose management      dose report              dose registry           dashboard, not the reader
AI triage            result object, flag      PACS and worklist       priority marker on worklist

The path in a deployment

  1. Images go from PACS or a router to the tool by DICOM store.
  2. The tool processes and creates a result.
  3. The result returns to PACS as a new object or series with the same study UID.
  4. A hanging protocol rule or a worklist rule makes the result visible.

Worked example

A lung CAD tool is installed. Radiologists say it does nothing. In the logs, the server receives the studies and runs. The results are sent back as a new series, but PACS places them in a separate study because the tool created a new study UID. The hanging protocol never finds them. The fix is to have the tool reuse the original study UID, and then add a protocol rule that displays the extra series. The algorithm was never the problem.

Decision support

At order entry it asks whether an exam is appropriate and can suggest an alternative. At protocoling it helps choose the right protocol and contrast. During interpretation, case comparison finds similar cases. Each is measured by whether the clinician sees it at the right moment.

Dose and contrast

The modality sends a dose report to a registry. The registry compares an exam to a reference and flags outliers. Contrast dose and injector data should be recorded in the study or in the chart, so a later reader knows what was given.

Modality structured reports

Ultrasound and DXA modalities can send measurements as structured reports. Reporting software pulls the values into the report so they are not retyped.
